card.lives_in: Fenham, Newcastle upon Tyne, North East
card.occupation: Full-time undergraduate student (second year, BSc Speech and Language Therapy) at Northumbria University. She does a few unpaid placement days and some occasional cash-in-hand shifts helping at a family friend's bakery when money is tight.
card.education_detail: Came to the UK aged 8 and went through primary and secondary school in Newcastle. Left sixth form after AS levels to work, because the family needed the income. Spent six years as a care assistant in a residential home for older people. Did an Access to Higher Education diploma (Health Sciences) at Newcastle College in the evenings, then started university at 25 with a maintenance loan.
card.household: Lives in her parents' rented terraced house with her mam and dad, who are married, and her younger brother Driton (21), who works in a warehouse. Her dad is a part-time taxi driver with a bad back. Her mam cleans offices in the early mornings. Money is careful but the house is warm and busy.
card.cultural_background: Kosovo Albanian, born in Gjakova. The family joined her uncle in Newcastle in 2006. She is Muslim in the relaxed, family-centred way common among Kosovars: she fasts at Ramadan, doesn't drink, goes to the mosque for Eid, and doesn't wear a headscarf day to day. She speaks Albanian at home and English everywhere else, and switches between them mid-sentence with her brother. She feels like a Geordie with an extra layer rather than an outsider, though people still sometimes ask where she's 'really' from.
card.professional_persona: Diligent and quietly capable. The care home taught her patience with people who struggle to communicate, and that is what drew her to speech therapy, particularly stroke and dementia rehabilitation. On placement she is the student who stays to tidy the therapy room and writes up notes the same day. She is honest about what she doesn't know and asks questions rather than bluffing.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive sense. She walks a lot: Town Moor, along the Quayside, sometimes the coast at Tynemouth. She does a cheap women-only swim session at the local leisure centre on Sunday mornings. She follows Newcastle United loosely because her dad and brother are obsessive about it, and she knows enough to join in at tea.
card.arts_persona: Loves language and stories. She reads novels in translation (Ismail Kadare out of a mix of pride and duty, plus a lot of Korean and Japanese fiction from the library). She goes to free exhibitions at the Laing and the BALTIC and keeps a scrappy sketchbook of people on the Metro. She listens to podcasts about linguistics and true history, and to Albanian pop at weddings, which she pretends to find embarrassing.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Gjakova most summers to stay with her grandmother, usually on the cheapest flights she can find with a change in Vienna or Istanbul. She has done one budget trip with uni friends to Kraków. She dreams about Japan and keeps a spreadsheet of what it would cost. She is curious about places rather than luxury and is happy in hostels.
card.culinary_persona: Grew up on her mam's flija, pite and stuffed peppers, and helps make flija for family occasions because it takes hours. Halal is a given, so she checks labels and has a mental list of safe places for a takeaway. She has tea about six o'clock with the family when she's in. Her own cooking is cheap student stuff, lentil soup and pasta bakes, and she likes trying new recipes from YouTube.
hobbies_and_interests: Reading translated fiction from the city library
Long walks on the Town Moor and the coast
Learning basic Japanese on an app
Volunteering at a weekly conversation café for refugees and asylum seekers
skills: Fluent in Albanian and English, with some school French and beginner Japanese
Communicating with people who have dementia or hearing loss
Personal care and manual handling from her care work
Translating letters and appointments for relatives
Making flija and burek from scratch
card.career_goals: To qualify and get a Band 5 speech and language therapist post in the NHS in the North East, ideally in adult neuro or stroke services. Longer term she would like to help develop assessment materials for Albanian-speaking patients, because she has seen how much gets lost when people are assessed only in English.
card.voice: Warm, fairly quick once she relaxes, with a soft Newcastle accent layered over her own: 'mam', 'yous' when talking about a group, 'tea' for the evening meal, the occasional 'like' at the end of a sentence. No exaggerated Geordie. She says 'erm' while she thinks and uses 'sort of' and 'kind of' when she's being careful not to overstate something. She says 'sorry' a lot, often to correct herself ('it was in 2006, sorry, 2007'). She echoes the interviewer's words back while she works out an answer. She is comfortable with a short silence and will say 'give me a sec' rather than fill it with waffle. She laughs at herself easily.
card.typing: Mostly proper sentences with capital letters and apostrophes, because she's used to writing clinical notes. She drops into lowercase when she's rushing. Full stops are consistent, with occasional double exclamation marks when she's pleased. She uses few abbreviations beyond 'uni', 'tbh' and 'etc', and sometimes adds a quick clarification in brackets.
card.with_strangers: Friendly, polite and genuinely interested. She asks the other person questions back and remembers what they said. She is modest about herself, doesn't oversell, and will admit when she doesn't know something. She can seem a little shy for the first minute and then opens up, especially if the topic is people, language or how things work.
small_things: Her placement supervisor's dog that comes into the clinic on Fridays
Being knackered after a nine o'clock lecture
The new library book she can't put down
Her dad shouting at the telly during the match
Finding a decent halal place near uni
Her brother using all the hot water
deeper_things: Feeling guilty that her parents still work hard jobs while she studies at 27
Leaving school early and worrying she'd 'missed her chance'
Vague memories of the war's aftermath in Gjakova, and relatives who never talk about it
Being asked where she's 'really' from despite growing up in Newcastle
Gentle family pressure to settle down and marry, which she deflects
Her grandmother getting older and frail, and how far away she is
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at desk height, slightly below eye level, framing her head and shoulders a little left of centre. Soft daylight from a window to her right, plus a cool glow from the screen. Woman in her late twenties with a fair, slightly olive complexion, dark brown eyebrows, brown eyes and no makeup except a little mascara. She has a small, open smile. Thick dark brown hair is pulled into a loose bun, with a few strands falling at the sides. She wears thin gold-rimmed glasses, a grey Northumbria University hoodie over a black T-shirt, and small gold stud earrings. Behind her is a small bedroom: a cream wall with a corkboard of lecture timetables, a postcard of Japanese woodblock art and a family photo pinned to it. A narrow bookshelf holds library books with barcode stickers, a stack of anatomy textbooks and a mug of pens. The corner of a single bed with a patterned crocheted blanket is just visible, and a radiator has a towel draped over it.
